findings.description: The five actual cache frames show the authored pleat silhouette collapsing into dense irregular crumpling by frame 16. The skirt remains uneven and distorted through frame 48 instead of recovering; the hem also exposes underlayers unevenly. This fails appearance and fit.

Directly inspected five native cloth-cache frame renders (1 neutral, 16 crouch, 32 sit, 40 prone, 48 neutral) with evaluated body and garment together. Frame 1 has a garment T-pose while body arms angle down. In frames 16 and 32 the body remains upright instead of matching crouch/sit and the jacket coverage is absent or displaced, exposing the torso. In frame 40 the body is horizontal while jacket remains upright and separated. This is a pose/bind or cache ordering defect, not evidence of safe pose fit.

Cache renders show garment details floating free around the body, with jacket sleeves and shoulder edges not following the posed arms, plus gray/pinched torso and lower-jacket artifacts. Rigid trim and non-cloth parts do not track the body/garment.

nextAction: Keep V162 rejected and prototype-only. Fix the garment/avatar rest-pose and bind/cache ordering mismatch first. Ensure non-cloth garment pieces, sleeve cuffs, rigid trims and waist pins follow their intended body or garment deformation. Then regenerate the same five native cache frames and directly inspect pose alignment, torso coverage, pleat recovery, hem and collision. Do not tune cloth shape parameters until the pose mapping is corrected. Fit, collision safety, weights, complete UVs, Shape Key response, Unity/VRChat execution, packaging and release remain unverified.
